title: A high fibre codimension constructible locus has fibrewise nonfull closure
statement: Let $T$ be a nonempty scheme of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum], and put $D=\dim T$. Let $q:X\to T$ be a smooth surjective separated algebraic-space morphism of finite presentation, all of whose geometric fibres are pure of one dimension $r\geq0$. For algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], smoothness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; finite presentation also requires quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness, and separatedness means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. A group algebraic space is an algebraic space with multiplication, inverse and identity morphisms over its base satisfying the group identities, without a commutativity assumption. A geometric fibre is the base change to an algebraically closed field at a point of the base; integral means reduced, irreducible and nonempty. Give point spaces the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology], and use topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with the empty subset of dimension $-\infty$. Let $Z\subseteq|X|$ be constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset], and let $c$ be an integer with $c>D$. Suppose that, for every geometric point $t$ of $T$, the closure in $|X_t|$ of the inverse image of $Z$ has dimension at most $r-c$. Let $\overline Z$ be the closure in $|X|$. Then $\overline Z$ contains no whole geometric fibre of $q$. Consequently the open subspace $W=X\setminus\overline Z$ [def-a1-space-open-subspace] is smooth and surjective over $T$. This assertion does not require $q$ proper or $Z$ closed, and makes no claim that $\overline Z$ commutes with base change.

source.place: Lemma 4.6, printed p.144, final dimension-counting sentence: if n-g exceeds dim S the closure of the bad locus cannot contain the special fibre. This is the constructible-locus dimension estimate isolated from the group argument. Supporting dimension formula: Stacks morphisms.tex Tag 02JU (lemma-dimension-formula), and spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 0BAX (lemma-dimension-formula-general), on finite-type arithmetic bases. Local Deligne PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Put $n=r-c$. Since $T$ is nonempty and $c>\dim T$, $D=\dim T$ is finite and nonnegative. If $n<0$, the hypothesis makes the inverse image of $Z$ in every geometric fibre empty: a nonempty space has a length-zero irreducible closed chain. Any point of $Z$, represented by a field-valued point of $X$, persists after taking an algebraic closure of that field and would give a point of one of those inverse images. Thus $Z=\varnothing$; then $W=X$ proves both conclusions. Henceforth assume $n\geq0$.

source.place: Tag 0055, definition-Krull, and the empty-locus case of the dimension count; algebraic closures: fields.tex Tag 09GT.

proof.text: The arithmetic finite-type hypothesis makes $T$ Noetherian. Since $q$ is quasi-compact and $T$ is quasi-compact, $|X|$ is quasi-compact: take finitely many affine opens of $T$ and finite subcovers on their inverse images. Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $p:U\to X$ with $U$ affine. The composite $f=q p:U\to T$ is smooth, surjective, and locally of finite type, by the chartwise calculus. Thus $U$ is locally Noetherian; being affine it is quasi-compact, and its point space is Noetherian by the cited topology theorem (applied also to schemes as algebraic spaces).

source.place: Tags 03H6 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine-cover) and 04ZF (Noetherian point topology); morphisms.tex Tag 01T6 for local Noetherianity.

proof.text: In a Noetherian space every open is quasi-compact: among finite unions from an open covering choose a maximal union, using stabilization of ascending opens; if it is not the whole open, adjoining a covering member increases it. Consequently every inverse image under $f$ of an affine open of $T$ is quasi-compact. Since $f$ is locally of finite type, it is of finite type. Its ordinary and geometric fibres are therefore finite-type schemes over their fields. They are separated: $U$ is affine and hence separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, and the relative diagonal of $f$ is the pullback of the absolute diagonal of $U$ along $U\times_TU\to U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}U$; base change gives the same assertion for its fibres.

source.place: Noetherian ascending-open condition; morphisms.tex finite-type base change. The relative diagonal calculation is from the definition of separatedness.

proof.text: Let $E=|p|^{-1}(Z)$ and $H=\overline E\subseteq|U|$. Constructibility expresses $Z$ as a finite union of locally closed subsets; continuity of $|p|$ therefore gives the same kind of expression for $E$. Since $p$ is open and continuous, $H=|p|^{-1}(\overline Z)$. Indeed continuity gives one inclusion, and for $u\in|p|^{-1}(\overline Z)$ every open neighbourhood $N$ of $u$ has open image $p(N)$ meeting $Z$, so $N$ meets $E$. Give $H$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure. Its map $H\to T$ is locally of finite type: its inclusion in $U$ is an immersion and hence locally of finite type, and compose with $f$.

source.place: Constructible finite locally closed decomposition and the neighbourhood proof of inverse image of closure under an open continuous map; schemes.tex reduced induced closed subscheme.

proof.text: Fix $t\in T$, put $k=\kappa(t)$, and choose an algebraic closure $\Omega/k$. Write $U_t$, $U_{\bar t}$, and $X_{\bar t}$ for the fibres, and $E_t,E_{\bar t},Z_{\bar t}$ for the inverse images of $E,E,Z$. (Thus $E_{\bar t}=p_{\bar t}^{-1}(Z_{\bar t})$.) The map $p_{\bar t}:U_{\bar t}\to X_{\bar t}$ is surjective etale. Let $B$ be the reduced closed subspace of $X_{\bar t}$ supported on $\overline{Z_{\bar t}}$; by hypothesis $\dim|B|\leq n$. It is separated, hence quasi-separated: its diagonal is obtained from the diagonal of the separated space $X_{\bar t}$ by the closed-subspace base-change calculation. The scheme $V=U_{\bar t}\times_{X_{\bar t}}B$ is etale over $B$. On each scheme chart of $B$, etale maps are locally quasi-finite by the cited etale lemma and etale composition. The source-dimension inequality for locally quasi-finite maps therefore gives $\dim V\leq\dim|B|\leq n$. The closed support of $V$ in $U_{\bar t}$ contains $E_{\bar t}$, hence also its closure.

For later comparisons use the following direct chain argument: if $A\subseteq B$ are subspaces, taking closures in $B$ of a strict chain of irreducible closed subsets of $A$ keeps it irreducible, closed, and strict, since intersecting these closures with $A$ recovers the original chain. Hence $\dim A\leq\dim B$; homeomorphisms preserve dimension by transporting chains both ways. Applied to the closed support in the previous step, this gives $\dim\overline{E_{\bar t}}\leq n$.

source.place: Tag 0055, definition-Krull; the chain proof of subspace monotonicity and homeomorphism invariance is written out here.

proof.text: Let $A_t$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme on $\overline{E_t}\subset U_t$. It is separated and of finite type over $k$: its inclusion is a closed immersion (locally finite type, with quasi-compact inverse images of affine opens), and $U_t$ is separated of finite type. The scalar-extension projection $v:U_{\bar t}\to U_t$ is open by universal openness over a field. The neighbourhood argument of step 4 gives $v^{-1}(\overline{E_t})=\overline{v^{-1}(E_t)}=\overline{E_{\bar t}}$. The closed-support base-change theorem identifies this inverse image with the point space of $(A_t)_\Omega$. Field-extension dimension invariance, applied to the separated finite-type scheme $A_t$ viewed as an algebraic space, now gives $\dim A_t=\dim(A_t)_\Omega\leq n$. This uses openness only for this field extension, not a closure identity for an arbitrary base change.

source.place: Tag 0383, lemma-scheme-over-field-universally-open; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 04NS, lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03IQ for the closed support.

proof.text: The closed subset $H$ of the Noetherian scheme $U$ has finitely many irreducible components $C_i$, with generic points $\eta_i$. Each $\eta_i$ belongs to $E$. To check this, remove the other components to obtain an open subset of $H$ containing $\eta_i$ and contained in $C_i$; density of $E$ in $H$ then makes $E\cap C_i$ dense in $C_i$. Express this intersection as a finite union of locally closed subsets. Irreducibility forces one of their closures to be all of $C_i$. That piece is open in its closure, so contains a dense open of $C_i$, and thus contains its generic point. This proves the claim without making any assertion about closure in a fibre.

source.place: Tag 005K, lemma-generic-point-in-constructible, with its finite-locally-closed proof written out; the finite-component isolation is explicit.

proof.text: Fix a generic point $\eta$ of $H$ and put $t=f(\eta)$. By step 8 its corresponding point $u_t\in U_t$ lies in $E_t$, so its irreducible closed point closure is contained in $|A_t|$ and has dimension at most $n$ by steps 6 and 7. The finite-type-over-a-field point-closure formula identifies its dimension with $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(t)}\kappa_{U_t}(u_t)$. The fibre-point residue-field formula gives $\kappa_{U_t}(u_t)=\kappa_U(\eta)$ compatibly over $\kappa(t)$: in that formula the tensor product is $\kappa_U(\eta)\otimes_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(t)\simeq\kappa_U(\eta)$. The closed immersion $H\hookrightarrow U$ induces an isomorphism on residue fields. Thus every component generic point of $H$ satisfies $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(t)}\kappa_H(\eta)\leq n$.

source.place: Tag 0B1C, item-dimension-irreducible-trdeg in lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic; schemes.tex fibre-point residue-field formula.

proof.text: Apply the generic-residue-field dimension bound to $H\to T$. Its target is locally Noetherian by step 2, its morphism is locally of finite type by step 4, and step 9 supplies the bound at every irreducible-component generic point. With $d=D$ and $n=r-c$ it gives $\dim H\leq D+r-c<r$. Empty $H$ is included in the same inequality.

source.place: Tag 0BAG, lemma-alteration-dimension-general, with the pointwise hypothesis established in step 9.

proof.text: If $\overline Z$ contained all of a geometric fibre $X_{\bar t}$ over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$, step 4 and closed-support base change would make the closed immersion $H_{\bar t}\hookrightarrow U_{\bar t}$ have full underlying support. The geometric atlas dimension theorem gives $\dim U_{\bar t}=\dim|X_{\bar t}|=r$, since that fibre is nonempty and pure of dimension $r$. On the other hand, for $t$ its underlying point, the field-extension inequality gives $\dim H_{\bar t}\leq\dim H_t$, and the ordinary fibre homeomorphism identifies $|H_t|$ with a subspace of $|H|$, of dimension at most $\dim H$ by step 6. Here $H_t$ is locally of finite type over $\kappa(t)$ by base change. Thus $r=\dim H_{\bar t}\leq\dim H<r$, a contradiction. The argument covers arbitrary algebraically closed extensions, not only the closures chosen in step 5.

source.place: Tag 0A4J, lemma-dimension-decent-space; algebra.tex Tag 00P3 for field extension; schemes.tex ordinary fibre topology.

proof.text: The complement $W$ is an open subspace. On etale scheme charts its map to $T$ is the restriction of a smooth scheme morphism to an open subscheme, hence smooth by the cited open-immersion composition theorem; smoothness of $W\to T$ is tested on these charts by the chartwise calculus. For surjectivity use the chart test of the chartwise calculus for the map $W\to T$, which is representable by algebraic spaces: let $T'\to T$ be a morphism from a scheme and $U'\to W\times_TT'$ a surjective etale scheme chart. For $t'\in T'$ over $t\in T$, choose an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ containing $\kappa(t')$; the geometric fibre of $W$ over the resulting geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ is nonempty by step 11. The point-space image/base-change criterion, applied first to $W\to T$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T'\to T$, and then to $W\to T$ and $T'\to T$, puts $t'$ in the image of $|W\times_TT'|\to|T'|$. The chart $U'\to W\times_TT'$ is representable surjective, so its point map is surjective by the same calculus; hence $U'\to T'$ is surjective, and $W\to T$ is surjective. These statements also handle the case $Z=\varnothing$ separated out in step 1.
